property_summary: For any admissible caller, calling owned() must leave the owner state unchanged (owned() is a read-only op for owner), but the mutant sets owner = msg.sender, so c.owner() differs after the call.

Calling owned() may only succeed for the current owner and, whether it succeeds or reverts, must never change the owner state; the mutant sets owner = msg.sender inside owned(), so for any caller different from the owner the mutant both succeeds and overwrites owner, which the reference never does.

For any non-zero caller, invoking owned() (which reverts for non-owners but otherwise must be side-effect free) leaves c.owner() unchanged at address(0); the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender, breaking the invariant.

For any admissible caller, once ownership is transferred to that caller, a call to owned() succeeds and must leave the owner state exactly as it was; the test drives owned() through the public surface and asserts ok && c.owner() == actor, which the reference always satisfies.

Rule: after transferring ownership to any address n, calling owned() from any caller (whether it succeeds or reverts) must never alter the owner, so c.owner() stays n; the mutant sets owner = msg.sender inside owned(), so any caller other than n breaks it.
